conflict_topics: fair access to stove (late arrival vs frequent cookers)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants offered concrete, operational solutions (whiteboard, 45-minute slots) rather than only abstract rules.
Requests and concessions were proportional and role-based (A notes cooking schedule; D requests fairness due to late arrival).
Minor repetition of the extractor/open-window/wash request but it helped secure explicit agreement rather than creating noise.
evaluation.final_reason: Housemates agreed concrete, mutually-acceptable rules and a scheduling system. Key lines: Agent A proposed washing and a rule: "whoever cooks washes their things, and we split basics like soap and gas." Agent D requested scheduling: "can we have a simple whiteboard to book stove slots so I get a fair chance?" Agent A implemented it: "I'll put it on the kitchen wall next to the stove, at eye level. Slots 45 minutes each — start tonight; swap with someone if you need more time." Agent C and A then confirmed practice for the evening: "Agreed. We'll run the extractor, open the window, and wash pans straight away tonight." "Good — let's stick to it tonight." These statements show who adjusted what (A agreed to install the board and follow wash rule; others accepted the 45-minute slots and extractor/window practice) and that the final outstanding demand (nighttime odor control and slotting) was accepted by all.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially defended frequent cooking as a break but quickly accepted rules, agreed to wash the pan immediately and to install the whiteboard (softened position).
Agent B: maintained the need to eliminate smell before sleep and repeatedly asked for extractor/window/wash; persisted until others explicitly agreed (position held until acceptance).
Agent C: moved from complaint about the unwashed pan to proposing the washing/extractor rule and swap option (from complaint to constructive proposer).
Agent D: introduced a new concern (fair stove access) and accepted the group's rule and the 45-minute slot compromise.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B: "The real problem is the smell — can we avoid strong-smelling cooking on weeknights, or at least always run the extractor, open the window and wash pans straight away?" Agent A: "I'll wash that pan now. I cook most nights — it's my break after work. Let's agree: whoever cooks washes their things, and we split basics like soap and gas." (A offers a rule and washes the pan; B's need for smell gone before sleep remains a practical incompatibility.)

Agent C: "...whoever cooks washes their own stuff straight away, and run the extractor and open the window for strong smells. If you're too tired, ask someone to swap..." Agent D: "One request: I get home late on weeknights — can we have a simple whiteboard to book stove slots so I get a fair chance?" (C supports washing/extractor; D introduces a new scheduling fairness demand.)

Agent A: "Okay — whiteboard for stove slots sounds fair. Let's agree: whoever cooks washes their things straight away, run the extractor and open the window for strong smells..." Agent D: "Okay, that's fine. Who will put up the whiteboard and where should we put it? When should we start using it?" (Agreement on principles but operational details remain open.)

Agent A: "I can put up the whiteboard by the kitchen wall next to the stove. We'll start using it tonight." Agent D: "Okay, start tonight. I'll book my slot when I get home. Where exactly will you put the board, and how long are the slots?" (Location promised but slot length still unresolved.)

Agent A: "I'll put it on the kitchen wall next to the stove, at eye level. Slots 45 minutes each — start tonight; swap with someone if you need more time." Agent B: "Okay, whiteboard and 45-minute slots work. Can we all agree to run the extractor, open the window and wash pans straight away tonight?" (Slots specified and accepted; the immediate-night practice is still awaiting explicit agreement.)

Agent C: "Agreed. We'll run the extractor, open the window, and wash pans straight away tonight. If you can't, swap or ask someone to wash." Agent A: "Good — let's stick to it tonight." (All housemates explicitly accept the concrete measures for tonight and the scheduling rule.)

substantive_insights: Main tension was between convenience of the frequent cook (A) and the sleep/odor needs of others (B), resolved by process rules rather than banning cooking.
Scheduling (whiteboard slots) is an effective compromise to balance late arrivals and frequent cooks.
A clear rule assigning responsibility for immediate washing of one’s own cookware addresses the shared-pan cleanliness problem.
Splitting basics (soap/gas) removes a potential source of free-riding and was accepted without dispute.
